units.id: mission:Sol-Bound Shuttle|	Upon entering the sprawling spaceport, you notice that a group of factory workers are talking to a captain. As you get closer, you see that the captain's flagship, a Shuttle that has seen better days, lacks a hyperdrive.|624|0
units.english: Upon entering the sprawling spaceport, you notice that a group of factory workers are talking to a captain. As you get closer, you see that the captain's flagship, a Shuttle that has seen better days, lacks a hyperdrive.
units.italian: Entrando nello spazioporto immenso, noti che un gruppo di operai di fabbrica sta parlando con una capitana. Quando ti avvicini, vedi che la sua nave ammiraglia, uno Shuttle che ha conosciuto giorni migliori, è priva di iperguida.

units.id: mission:Sol-Bound Shuttle|	"Where's your hyperdrive?"|626|0
units.english: "Where's your hyperdrive?"
units.italian: "Dov'è la tua iperguida?"

units.id: mission:Sol-Bound Shuttle|	"How are you going to travel anywhere with that ship?"|627|0
units.english: "How are you going to travel anywhere with that ship?"
units.italian: "Come farai a viaggiare da qualche parte con quella nave?"

units.id: mission:Sol-Bound Shuttle|	(Go back to my ship.)|628|0
units.english: (Go back to my ship.)
units.italian: (Torna alla mia nave.)

units.id: mission:Sol-Bound Shuttle|	The captain laughs. "Most pilots are the adventurous type. Not me. I make a pretty decent haul just flying people from Earth to Mars and back. Occasionally I do trips to the Moon for tourists." You notice that she uses the archaic term for Luna. Must be a local expression.|630|0
units.english: The captain laughs. "Most pilots are the adventurous type. Not me. I make a pretty decent haul just flying people from Earth to Mars and back. Occasionally I do trips to the Moon for tourists." You notice that she uses the archaic term for Luna. Must be a local expression.
units.italian: La capitana ride. "La maggior parte dei piloti è del tipo avventuroso. Io no. Faccio un buon gruzzolo solo portando gente dalla Terra a Marte e ritorno. Ogni tanto faccio viaggi sulla Luna per i turisti." Noti che usa il termine arcaico per Luna. Dev'essere un'espressione locale.

units.id: mission:Sol-Bound Shuttle|	"Doesn't that get boring?"|632|0
units.english: "Doesn't that get boring?"
units.italian: "Non diventa noioso?"

units.id: mission:Sol-Bound Shuttle|	"Is there really enough travel within Sol that you can make a living off of it?"|634|0
units.english: "Is there really enough travel within Sol that you can make a living off of it?"
units.italian: "C'è davvero abbastanza traffico dentro il Sol perché tu ci possa vivere?"

units.id: mission:Sol-Bound Shuttle|	"You'd be surprised. There's a lot of people in this system after all, and a lot of those people have enough money to leave Earth but not enough to leave Sol. It's a nice niche I've carved out for myself."|635|0
units.english: "You'd be surprised. There's a lot of people in this system after all, and a lot of those people have enough money to leave Earth but not enough to leave Sol. It's a nice niche I've carved out for myself."
units.italian: "Rimarresti sorpreso. In questo sistema c'è molta gente, dopotutto, e molta di quella gente ha abbastanza soldi per lasciare la Terra ma non abbastanza per lasciare il Sol. È una bella nicchia che mi sono ritagliata."

units.id: mission:Sol-Bound Shuttle|	"For you, maybe. I can tell by your accent that you've done a bit of travelling from your home planet. I like staying closer to home, though. With all the instability in the galaxy - pirates, aliens, and who knows what else - staying in Sol keeps me safe. Call me paranoid, but being in a place where I don't have to worry about that is something I value." She eyes a ship to the side that's having its hull repaired. The damage appears to have been inflicted by a beam weapon.|638|0
units.english: "For you, maybe. I can tell by your accent that you've done a bit of travelling from your home planet. I like staying closer to home, though. With all the instability in the galaxy - pirates, aliens, and who knows what else - staying in Sol keeps me safe. Call me paranoid, but being in a place where I don't have to worry about that is something I value." She eyes a ship to the side that's having its hull repaired. The damage appears to have been inflicted by a beam weapon.
units.italian: "Per te, forse. Dal tuo accento capisco che hai viaggiato un po' dal tuo pianeta natale. Io però preferisco restare vicina a casa. Con tutta l'instabilità della galassia, pirati, alieni e chissà cos'altro, restare nel Sol mi tiene al sicuro. Dimmi che sono paranoica, ma stare in un posto dove non devo preoccuparmene è qualcosa che tengo." Guarda di lato una nave a cui stanno riparando lo scafo. Il danno sembra essere stato causato da un'arma a raggio.

units.id: mission:Sol-Bound Shuttle|	You say your goodbyes as you board your ships. Although you are both captains, the trajectory of your lives have taken very different courses.|640|0
units.english: You say your goodbyes as you board your ships. Although you are both captains, the trajectory of your lives have taken very different courses.
units.italian: Vi salutate mentre salite sulle rispettive navi. Anche se siete entrambi capitani, le traiettorie delle vostre vite hanno preso strade molto diverse.

units.id: mission:Earth Day Blackout|As you follow the tracking beacons towards Earth's central spaceport, you realize there's something very off. What was the bustling spaceport city is now completely still, and even though it is near midnight, the supertall buildings and skyscrapers are curiously dark; not a light is on for kilometers.|661|0
units.english: As you follow the tracking beacons towards Earth's central spaceport, you realize there's something very off. What was the bustling spaceport city is now completely still, and even though it is near midnight, the supertall buildings and skyscrapers are curiously dark; not a light is on for kilometers.
units.italian: Mentre segui i ripetitori di tracciamento verso lo spazioporto centrale della Terra, ti rendi conto che c'è qualcosa di molto strano. Quella che era una città-spazioporto piena di vita ora è completamente immobile, e anche se è quasi mezzanotte i grattacieli enormi sono stranamente bui; non c'è una luce accesa per chilometri.

units.id: mission:Earth Day Blackout|	Despite this, the spaceport seems to still be operational, because the automated procedures of signing landing documents, refueling, and checking your ship's spaceworthiness are completed as you land. In the spaceport terminal, there are wax candles spaced out to bring some light into the now dark corridors. It's a strange sight for the most populated planet in human space.|662|0
units.english: Despite this, the spaceport seems to still be operational, because the automated procedures of signing landing documents, refueling, and checking your ship's spaceworthiness are completed as you land. In the spaceport terminal, there are wax candles spaced out to bring some light into the now dark corridors. It's a strange sight for the most populated planet in human space.
units.italian: Nonostante questo, lo spazioporto sembra ancora operativo, perché le procedure automatiche di firma dei documenti di atterraggio, rifornimento e controllo dell'idoneità spaziale della nave si completano mentre atterri. Nel terminale dello spazioporto ci sono candele di cera distanziate per portare un po' di luce nei corridoi ora bui. È una vista strana per il pianeta più popoloso dello spazio umano.

units.id: mission:Earth Day Blackout|	(Find someone and ask.)|664|0
units.english: (Find someone and ask.)
units.italian: (Trova qualcuno e chiedi.)

units.id: mission:Earth Day Blackout|	(The blackout will probably pass.)|665|0
units.english: (The blackout will probably pass.)
units.italian: (Il blackout passerà probabilmente.)

units.id: mission:Earth Day Blackout|	You approach an information desk in the terminal's atrium that, given the situation, doesn't seem to be as busy as expected. After a moment you get to the attendant behind the counter.|671|0
units.english: You approach an information desk in the terminal's atrium that, given the situation, doesn't seem to be as busy as expected. After a moment you get to the attendant behind the counter.
units.italian: Ti avvicini a un banco informazioni nell'atrio del terminale che, data la situazione, non sembra così affollato come ci si aspetterebbe. Dopo un momento arrivi all'addetto dietro il banco.

units.id: mission:Earth Day Blackout|	"What's with the blackout?"|673|0
units.english: "What's with the blackout?"
units.italian: "Che succede con il blackout?"

units.id: mission:Earth Day Blackout|	"When is the blackout going to be fixed?"|674|0
units.english: "When is the blackout going to be fixed?"
units.italian: "Quando verrà risolto il blackout?"

units.id: mission:Earth Day Blackout|	The attendant chuckles to himself. "I should've expected that question from your accent. Today's Earth Day, when all the cities of Earth - and I mean all of them - participate in a total blackout. Even the Parliament building was out today. It makes us think about our origins; that we once lived on the soil without electricity, all confined to just this one planet here, divided and uncertain. Of course, people like me still have to keep working, but for other people it's a day off to enjoy what little wildlife and Earth us Earthlings have left, ironically. Do you have any other questions?|675|0
units.english: The attendant chuckles to himself. "I should've expected that question from your accent. Today's Earth Day, when all the cities of Earth - and I mean all of them - participate in a total blackout. Even the Parliament building was out today. It makes us think about our origins; that we once lived on the soil without electricity, all confined to just this one planet here, divided and uncertain. Of course, people like me still have to keep working, but for other people it's a day off to enjoy what little wildlife and Earth us Earthlings have left, ironically. Do you have any other questions?
units.italian: L'addetto ridacchia. "Avrei dovuto aspettarmelo, una domanda così, dal tuo accento. Oggi è la Giornata della Terra, quando tutte le città della Terra, e dico tutte, partecipano a un blackout totale. Anche l'edificio del Parlamento oggi era spento. Ci fa pensare alle nostre origini; che un tempo vivevamo sulla terraferma senza elettricità, tutti confinati su questo unico pianeta, divisi e incerti. Certo, gente come me deve continuare a lavorare, ma per gli altri è un giorno libero per godersi quel poco di natura e di Terra che noi terrestri ci siamo lasciati, ironicamente. Hai altre domande?

units.id: mission:Earth Day Blackout|	"When did this tradition start?"|677|0
units.english: "When did this tradition start?"
units.italian: "Quando è iniziata questa tradizione?"

units.id: mission:Earth Day Blackout|	"Thank you for telling me."|678|0
units.english: "Thank you for telling me."
units.italian: "Grazie per avermelo detto."

units.id: mission:Earth Day Blackout|	"Well, my old history class tells me that the first Earth Day was around the 20th century, a few years after we landed on the Moon for the first time. Back then, there were a bunch of conflicts and disputes over resources and how we were fighting all over and digging it all up to power all those dirty, primitive cars, power plants, and factories we had back then. So as a show of unity against that people started celebrating Earth's natural beauty by bringing us back to our past."|680|0
units.english: "Well, my old history class tells me that the first Earth Day was around the 20th century, a few years after we landed on the Moon for the first time. Back then, there were a bunch of conflicts and disputes over resources and how we were fighting all over and digging it all up to power all those dirty, primitive cars, power plants, and factories we had back then. So as a show of unity against that people started celebrating Earth's natural beauty by bringing us back to our past."
units.italian: "Beh, la mia vecchia lezione di storia mi dice che la prima Giornata della Terra è stata intorno al XX secolo, qualche anno dopo che siamo atterrati sulla Luna per la prima volta. Allora c'erano un mucchio di conflitti e dispute per le risorse e su come ci combattevamo dappertutto e scavavamo tutto per alimentare tutte quelle auto sporche e primitive, le centrali e le fabbriche che avevamo allora. Così, come dimostrazione di unità contro tutto questo, la gente ha cominciato a celebrare la bellezza naturale della Terra riportandoci al nostro passato."

units.id: mission:Earth Day Blackout|	As he finishes, the ceiling lights flash back on. "Ah, well, there you go. Too bad I missed the celebrations, but that's the end of Earth Day and my night shift. I hope you had a good Earth Day, and have a good night!"|681|0
units.english: As he finishes, the ceiling lights flash back on. "Ah, well, there you go. Too bad I missed the celebrations, but that's the end of Earth Day and my night shift. I hope you had a good Earth Day, and have a good night!"
units.italian: Appena finisce, le luci del soffitto si riaccendono. "Ah, ecco fatto. Peccato essermi perso i festeggiamenti, ma questa è la fine della Giornata della Terra e del mio turno di notte. Spero che tu abbia passato una buona Giornata della Terra, e buona notte!"

units.id: mission:Earth Day Blackout|	You approach a woman with a bunch of oversized bags clustered around her seat. She's tapping rapidly on her datapad, but nonetheless she looks up when you approach. "Excuse me, Captain, I was just trying to figure out when the metro starts up again. Do you know?"|685|0
units.english: You approach a woman with a bunch of oversized bags clustered around her seat. She's tapping rapidly on her datapad, but nonetheless she looks up when you approach. "Excuse me, Captain, I was just trying to figure out when the metro starts up again. Do you know?"
units.italian: Ti avvicini a una donna con un mucchio di borse oversize raggruppate intorno alla sedia. Sta picchiettando velocemente sul datapad, ma alza comunque lo sguardo quando ti avvicini. "Scusa, capitano, stavo cercando di capire quando riapre la metropolitana. Lo sai?"

units.id: mission:Earth Day Blackout|	"I know just as much as you, sorry."|687|0
units.english: "I know just as much as you, sorry."
units.italian: "Ne so quanto te, mi dispiace."

units.id: mission:Earth Day Blackout|	"Maybe it's to do with the blackout?"|688|0
units.english: "Maybe it's to do with the blackout?"
units.italian: "Forse ha a che fare con il blackout?"

units.id: mission:Earth Day Blackout|	"Ha, they shut everything down for Earth Day and then assume all us offworlders get the idea. What do you know..."|690|0
units.english: "Ha, they shut everything down for Earth Day and then assume all us offworlders get the idea. What do you know..."
units.italian: "Ah, spengono tutto per la Giornata della Terra e poi danno per scontato che tutti noi che veniamo da fuori lo capiamo. Chi l'avrebbe detto..."

units.id: mission:Earth Day Blackout|	"Earth Day?"|692|0
units.english: "Earth Day?"
units.italian: "Giornata della Terra?"

units.id: mission:Earth Day Blackout|	"Shut everything down?"|693|0
units.english: "Shut everything down?"
units.italian: "Spengono tutto?"

units.id: mission:Earth Day Blackout|	"Didn't you see what was happening outside on your way in? It's something to do with Earth Day. Back in those old days before humans were able to get off this planet, they were stuck in a chain of issues and disputes over energy. You know, they didn't have fusion reactors back then. Awfully primitive times.|694|0
units.english: "Didn't you see what was happening outside on your way in? It's something to do with Earth Day. Back in those old days before humans were able to get off this planet, they were stuck in a chain of issues and disputes over energy. You know, they didn't have fusion reactors back then. Awfully primitive times.
units.italian: "Non hai visto quello che succedeva fuori mentre entravi? Ha a che fare con la Giornata della Terra. In quei tempi antichi, prima che gli umani riuscissero a lasciare questo pianeta, erano bloccati in una catena di problemi e dispute sull'energia. Sai, allora non avevano reattori a fusione. Tempi terribilmente primitivi.

units.id: mission:Earth Day Blackout|label|697|0
units.english: way in
units.italian: way in

units.id: mission:Earth Day Blackout|	"Yes, I suppose you must have seen what's happening outside on your way in. It's something to do with Earth Day. Back in those old days before humans were able to get off this planet, they were stuck in a chain of issues and disputes over energy. You know, they didn't have fusion reactors back then. Awfully primitive times.|698|0
units.english: "Yes, I suppose you must have seen what's happening outside on your way in. It's something to do with Earth Day. Back in those old days before humans were able to get off this planet, they were stuck in a chain of issues and disputes over energy. You know, they didn't have fusion reactors back then. Awfully primitive times.
units.italian: "Sì, suppongo che tu abbia visto quello che succedeva fuori mentre entravi. Ha a che fare con la Giornata della Terra. In quei tempi antichi, prima che gli umani riuscissero a lasciare questo pianeta, erano bloccati in una catena di problemi e dispute sull'energia. Sai, allora non avevano reattori a fusione. Tempi terribilmente primitivi.

units.id: mission:Earth Day Blackout|	"So they decided that, on the 22nd of April each year, all of Earth would go into total blackout to symbolize that they didn't have enough energy to sustain themselves, and to remind them that the only way to advance was to keep pushing themselves forward, find new pathways to power, lest those blackouts became longer and more frequent. Fascinating, huh?"|701|0
units.english: "So they decided that, on the 22nd of April each year, all of Earth would go into total blackout to symbolize that they didn't have enough energy to sustain themselves, and to remind them that the only way to advance was to keep pushing themselves forward, find new pathways to power, lest those blackouts became longer and more frequent. Fascinating, huh?"
units.italian: "Così hanno deciso che, il 22 aprile di ogni anno, tutta la Terra sarebbe entrata in un blackout totale per simboleggiare che non avevano abbastanza energia per sostentarsi, e per ricordare loro che l'unico modo per avanzare era continuare a spingersi avanti, trovare nuove vie per l'energia, altrimenti quei blackout sarebbero diventati più lunghi e più frequenti. Affascinante, eh?"

units.id: mission:Earth Day Blackout|	"It seems a bit backwards."|703|0
units.english: "It seems a bit backwards."
units.italian: "Mi sembra un po' un passo indietro."

units.id: mission:Earth Day Blackout|	"It is fascinating, thanks."|704|0
units.english: "It is fascinating, thanks."
units.italian: "È affascinante, grazie."

units.id: mission:Earth Day Blackout|	"Well, perhaps. But Earth is like that sometimes. It's survived through so much, and without Earth Day to remind our ancestors that we must keep looking forward, maybe you wouldn't be in your fancy little spaceship, would you?"|706|0
units.english: "Well, perhaps. But Earth is like that sometimes. It's survived through so much, and without Earth Day to remind our ancestors that we must keep looking forward, maybe you wouldn't be in your fancy little spaceship, would you?"
units.italian: "Beh, forse. Ma la Terra è così a volte. È sopravvissuta a così tanto, e senza la Giornata della Terra per ricordare ai nostri antenati che dobbiamo continuare a guardare avanti, forse non saresti sulla tua graziosa navicella, vero?"

units.id: mission:Earth Day Blackout|	The lights in the spaceport turn back on as she says that, and she turns to look at her data pad again. "Oh, it's twelve o'clock. I've got to see if the metro's opened so I can get to my accommodation. Safe travels!"|707|0
units.english: The lights in the spaceport turn back on as she says that, and she turns to look at her data pad again. "Oh, it's twelve o'clock. I've got to see if the metro's opened so I can get to my accommodation. Safe travels!"
units.italian: Le luci dello spazioporto si riaccendono mentre lo dice, e lei si volta di nuovo verso il datapad. "Oh, è mezzanotte. Devo vedere se la metropolitana ha aperto per arrivare al mio alloggio. Buon viaggio!"

units.id: mission:Earth Day Blackout|	After the clock passes midnight, the lights in the spaceport come back on, followed by the signage and lights of the city surrounding it. A few workers come and snuff out the candles before putting them away in unseen closets.|711|0
units.english: After the clock passes midnight, the lights in the spaceport come back on, followed by the signage and lights of the city surrounding it. A few workers come and snuff out the candles before putting them away in unseen closets.
units.italian: Dopo che l'orologio supera la mezzanotte, le luci dello spazioporto si riaccendono, seguite dalle insegne e dalle luci della città intorno. Alcuni operai passano a spegnere le candele e poi le ripongono in armadi che non si vedono.
